title: the installer proof runs green on a Windows box
intention: test_installer.py is green on a Windows box, and where it is not, it names the Windows fact that blocks it.
why: Measured 2026-11-12 on akiendell: test_installer.py is red on a clean HEAD worktree: [ask_yn] expected 'no-branch' got '', [ask_yn] exit 127, [applied] expected applied got failed
traces_to: Law 3 and Law 8: a proof red on one box for a platform reason is not measuring the component; CP4 resolves the chafe.
how: Measure why bash runs ask_user.sh and the seam verify commands to exit 127 under this venv's python on Windows (candidate: the PATH bash or its sub-shell lacks a command the fixtures use); then fix the proof's or the installer's invocation. The red-first tooth is the existing proof, red on HEAD.

clauses.claim: test_installer.py's ask_yn and applied teeth are green on a Windows box
the same proof stays green on a posix box

decisions.text: D2: one proof, one tooth per clause; red first.

measured.saw: test_installer.py is red on a clean HEAD worktree: [ask_yn] expected 'no-branch' got '', [ask_yn] exit 127, [applied] expected applied got failed
measured.how: ran the proof in a detached git worktree at HEAD with the venv python; shutil.which('bash') is Git's bash and echo hi returns 0 there, so the cause is HYPOTHESIS

measured.saw: Three causes, each measured. (1) subprocess.run(['bash', ...]) from python on Windows resolves via CreateProcess to C:\Windows\System32\bash.exe, the WSL launcher, though shutil.which lists Git's bash first; it strips the backslashes from a Windows path (rc 127). (2) text=True writes 'Y\r\n' on Windows and ask_user.sh read 'Y\r'. (3) the applied tooth built 'test -f C:\Users\...' and bash ate the backslashes. Fixed: installer.bash_exe() (shutil.which) used by run_verify and the proof; ask_user.sh strips a trailing CR; the proof's commands use as_posix(). test_installer.py 13 teeth GREEN twice on Windows.
measured.how: python subprocess probes of both bashes, then test_installer.py before and after each fix
